candidates.attacker_control: The raw Content-Type request header of an unauthenticated HTTP request (attacker fully controls its value, including %{...} fragments), plus, for the alternate jakarta-stream parser, the multipart Content-Disposition filename/field names. No session, login, or action parameters are required, and the trigger occurs during request wrapping before an ActionMapping is resolved.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: 1) If a resource bundle defined struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException, the constant bundle text (not the attacker string) would be used; struts-messages.properties lines 34-36 define only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException, so the fallback is taken. 2) Dispatcher requires the literal substring 'multipart/form-data'; this is compatible with triggering the library rejection condition (which fires precisely when the value does not start with 'multipart/'). 3) OgnlUtil.checkEnableEvalExpression lines 361-365 with default struts.ognl.enableOGNLEvalExpression=false may block some OGNL 'eval chain' payload forms, and struts-default.xml lines 41-61 exclude java.lang./ognl/javax packages and several classes; these mitigate but do not remove the injection sink and do not constitute validation of the attacker string. 4) Other LocalizedTextUtil.findText call sites (ParametersInterceptor, AliasInterceptor, StaticParametersInterceptor, TokenHelper) pass constant default messages or constants as arguments, so no second request-controlled default-message path was found there. 5) Dispatcher.wrapRequest occurs before findActionMapping, so the trigger does not require a mapped upload action.
candidates.impact: Attacker-controlled OGNL expressions are evaluated inside the request-handling thread of an unauthenticated request for any URL handled by the Struts filter. This permits unintended expression evaluation against the OGNL value stack/application context (information disclosure, state manipulation, invocation of reachable objects). This class of flaw historically escalates to remote code execution when OGNL sandbox restrictions are bypassed; even without a sandbox bypass, the framework is evaluating untrusted request text as executable expression language. The alternate jakarta-stream parser provides an equivalent in-repo path driven by the multipart filename.
candidates.prerequisites: Deployment uses the default multipart parser (struts.multipart.parser=jakarta, default.properties line 69) and routes the request through the Struts filter (not an excluded/static path). The Content-Type value must contain the substring "multipart/form-data" (Dispatcher line 792) but must cause commons-fileupload to reject the request as non-multipart (value not starting with "multipart/"), so that FileUploadBase throws an exception whose message embeds the raw header. An ActionContext/value stack exists at that point because StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter creates it (line 104) before wrapRequest (line 106).
candidates.root_cause: LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() treats the caller-supplied fallback message as an expression template: line 729 runs TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack), which evaluates every ${...}/%{...} fragment through the OGNL value stack (TextParseUtil lines 154-169, stack.findValue at line 158). JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() (lines 115-119) passes the multipart exception's getMessage() as that fallback after a bundle lookup fails, and the multipart exception message contains the raw request Content-Type. The same flawed pattern exists in MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage() (lines 105-109) and JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage()/addFileSkippedError() (lines 510-514, 349-356). No bundle entry exists for the relevant exception keys, so the attacker-influenced string is always the one evaluated.
candidates.title: Attacker-controlled Content-Type reaches OGNL evaluation via multipart error-message fallback (JakartaMultiPartRequest -> LocalizedTextUtil)
candidates.trace: StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter.doFilter lines 103-106 -> PrepareOperations.wrapRequest line 148 -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest lines 791-795 (contains("multipart/form-data")) -> new MultiPartRequestWrapper lines 76-88 -> multi.parse (JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse lines 82-107) -> processUpload/parseRequest lines 121-179 -> ServletFileUpload.parseRequest throws FileUploadException embedding the request Content-Type -> catch at lines 86-106 -> buildErrorMessage lines 115-119 passes e.getMessage() as defaultMessage -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText(Class,...) lines 391-395 -> findText lines 448-593 (no resource-bundle entry for keys such as struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException; only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException exist in struts-messages.properties lines 34-36) -> getDefaultMessage lines 714-737 -> line 729 TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) -> OgnlTextParser.evaluate line 49 -> OgnlValueStack.findValue -> OgnlUtil/OGNL execution.
candidates.unverified: commons-fileupload 1.3.1 (declared in root pom lines 711-715) is a binary dependency not present in the snapshot; the assumption that its InvalidContentTypeException/FileUploadException message embeds the raw Content-Type value is based on the library's documented behavior and cannot be re-verified from these files. Whether default OGNL sandbox restrictions can be bypassed for full code execution was not tested and no payloads were executed. Line ranges are from the snapshot as read.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression-language (OGNL) injection / potential remote code execution

coverage_summary: Scope: 2,644 model-visible files; the filter reports no excluded sensitive paths, symlinks, or >5 MiB files, so the snapshot as listed is the audited scope. Files read or closely inspected: core dispatcher (Dispatcher, PrepareOperations, StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter, DefaultStaticContentLoader), all multipart parsers and wrappers (JakartaMultiPartRequest, JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest, MultiPartRequestWrapper), OGNL/expression utilities (LocalizedTextUtil, TextParseUtil, OgnlTextParser, OgnlUtil, OgnlValueStack, SecurityMemberAccess), action mapping (DefaultActionMapper, Restful2ActionMapper), interceptors (ParametersInterceptor, FileUploadInterceptor), TokenHelper, RequestMap, REST XStream handler, app config (struts-default.xml, default.properties, struts-messages*.properties, pom.xml). Pattern searches covered Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder, Class.forName, new URL/openStream, setAccessible, translateVariables/findText call sites, and bundle keys. Not exhaustively audited: most plugin modules (574 files under plugins/, e.g. embeddedjsp/Jasper copy, json/oval/cdi/osgi), showcase/portlet/rest-showcase application code, archetypes, tests, and bundled third-party libraries (commons-fileupload, OGNL, XStream, log4j2), whose sources are absent from the snapshot.
limitations: commons-fileupload 1.3.1, OGNL 3.1.4 and XStream 1.4.8 sources are not in the snapshot; dependency-level behavior (notably the exact multipart exception message content) is inferred from call sites and library usage, not read here.
No code, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were executed; the candidate is a source-level lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

The OGNL sandbox configured in struts-default.xml (excludedClasses/excludedPackageNames, enableOGNLEvalExpression=false) and OgnlUtil's eval-chain check were not tested for bypassability; code-execution impact is therefore stated as potential.
Line numbers refer to the snapshot files as read and may differ from upstream numbering.
Coverage is not exhaustive across all 2,644 files; low-signal areas (most plugins, apps, tests, embedded third-party copies) were sampled rather than fully audited.

rejected_leads.lead: plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java lines 43-50: createXStream() returns a plain unrestricted new XStream() and toObject() calls xstream.fromXML(in, target) on request body data (S2-052-class deserialization RCE with XStream 1.4.8).
rejected_leads.reason: Real risk, but it is confined to the optional REST plugin, requires an XML content-type request routed to that plugin and a suitable deserialization target/gadget, and was not verified against this snapshot's handler wiring; the core multipart OGNL path is default-enabled and stronger.

rejected_leads.lead: apps/showcase/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/showcase/source/ViewSourceAction.java lines 91-98: request-controllable config parameter reaches new URL(config).openStream() behind a weak startsWith(rootPath) check (SSRF/local file read when rootPath is null).
rejected_leads.reason: Sample showcase application code, not framework core; attacker control depends on deploying the showcase app and is lower impact than the framework expression injection.
The output path appears to come from plugin configuration/use, not from a request parameter; no attacker-controlled source was traced, so it is only a hardening opportunity.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultActionMapper dynamic method invocation via method:/action: prefixes (lines 136-168).
rejected_leads.reason: DefaultActionMapper defaults allowDynamicMethodCalls=false and allowActionPrefix=false; exploitation would require a non-default configuration, so this is weaker than the default-enabled multipart path.
Examined but no concrete request-controlled value reaching OGNL evaluation was traced with this snapshot's defaults; left as unconfirmed leads rather than findings.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Struts 2.5-SNAPSHOT source tree (2,644 model-visible files), focusing on the request-dispatch/multipart path, the OGNL expression machinery, action mapping, upload handling, static content serving, and the REST plugin. One candidate meets the evidence bar: a pre-fix multipart error-message path that feeds attacker-controlled request text into OGNL evaluation (the S2-045-class flaw). The multipart exception text (derived from the raw, attacker-supplied Content-Type, and for the alternate parser from the multipart filename) is passed as the "default message" to LocalizedTextUtil, whose fallback branch evaluates ${...}/%{...} through TextParseUtil onto the OGNL value stack. This is reachable pre-authentication on the default `jakarta` multipart parser before action mapping, so any path handled by the Struts filter can trigger it. No other issue examined had comparable attacker control, default configuration, and impact; the XStream deserialization in the REST plugin and the showcase-app URL fetch are noted as rejected leads.
